newsitem.title: UK: June may be wettest this century in Britain.
newsitem.headline: June may be wettest this century in Britain.

text.p: The Meteorological Office said on Monday this month could be the wettest June this century in England and Wales.
With 24 hours left, 126.5 mm of rain had fallen, just 2.5 mm below the record set in June 1982. June is already the wettest month since January 1995.
But the government's Environment Agency said the heavy rain in June had not ended drought conditions in Britain with groundwater levels still at record lows in many areas.
The period between April 1995 and March 1997 was the driest 24-month period for more than 200 years.

"This rain comes after 2-1/2 years of exceptionally dry weather, so we are still effectively missing six months of winter rainfall which is essential for refilling groundwater supplies," the agency said in a statement.

"The areas that rely on groundwater are, therefore, still suffering from drought." But it said the recent rain had reduced consumer demand and was also good news for the environment, recharging river levels.
The bad weather this month has disrupted major sporting events and led to localised flooding.
